analysis_steps.goal: Derive binary orbit from archival astrometry

method.value: Relative astrometry by least-squares PSF fitting; orbit fit with orbitize! (ptemcee) and orbfit_lib

evidence.quote: we employed the `orbitize!` package (cite: Blunt20) in combination with the parallel-tempered package `ptemcee` (cite: Vousden16)

key_parameters.value: 10 temperatures, 100 walkers, 80000 steps, first half burn-in

evidence.quote: We performed each fit with 10 temperatures and 100 walkers per temperature, advanced the chains 80000 steps, cut the first half as an extended burn-in
We therefore fixed the parallax of the system to 6.91 mas, which is the mean estimate for the L1551 cloud (cite: Galli19).

fitting.value: Uniform priors on e, omega, Omega, tau0; log-uniform a; sine-uniform i; Gaussian prior on total mass

evidence.quote: we employ uniform ($e$, $\omega$, $\Omega$ and $\tau_0$), log-uniform ($a$) and sine-uniform ($i$) priors.

validation.value: Compared MCMC and least-squares results; chain inspection for convergence

evidence.quote: Inspection of the chain evolution confirms that they have reached convergence.

method.value: 3D SPH with PHANTOM, one-fluid dust, sink-particle stars, coplanar and 30 deg misaligned orbits, evolved up to 3000/1500 orbits

evidence.quote: We perform two sets of gas and dust 3D hydrodynamic simulations using the SPH (Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics) code `PHANTOM`

key_parameters.value: 1e6 SPH particles, Rout=800 au, disc mass 0.12 Msun, dust-to-gas 0.01, 1 mm grains, alpha_SS=0.005

evidence.quote: The system is surrounded by a disc of 1$\times 10^6$ SPH particles

assumptions.value: Locally isothermal, T=20 K (R/300 au)^-0.9; no disc self-gravity; no circumstellar discs

evidence.quote: We neglect the disc self-gravity, as our disc mass results in a gravitationally stable disc.

validation.value: Benchmarked against earlier gas-only results (Cazzoletti 2017, Aly 2018)

evidence.quote: We summarise here previous findings for bench-marking our gas dynamics results in the overlapping parameter space

method.value: CaSh computes cavity eccentricity and semi-major axis; cavity edge at 50% of peak surface density

evidence.quote: the semi-major axis of the inner cavity is defined as the radius $R_{\textrm{mid}}$, at which the surface density becomes half its maximum value

analysis_steps.goal: Synthetic images and comparison with ALMA/SPHERE

method.value: MCFOST Monte Carlo RT at 1300 and 1.67 micron, convolved with observed beam, visually compared with ALMA Band 6 and SPHERE images

evidence.quote: We post-process the selected snapshots of all the simulations using `MCFOST`

key_parameters.value: 1.3e8 photon packets; d=145 pc; i=37 deg; PA=97 deg; dust mass fixed to 1e-3 Msun

evidence.quote: we compute the temperature of our models by using $1.3 \times 10^8$ photon packets

assumptions.value: DIANA dust: 60% silicates, 15% amorphous carbon, 25% porosity; dn/da ∝ a^-3.5, amin 0.03 um, amax 3.5 mm; Mie+EMT

evidence.quote: We assume a chemical composition of 60% silicates, 15% amorphous carbon, and 25% porosity (in volume ratios)

validation.value: Visual comparison of cavity size, ring size, star position and streams

evidence.loc: What is the most likely configuration for GG Tau A?
evidence.quote: We conclude that the misaligned configuration on short times is the best match of GG Tau A.

results_numeric.quantity: Coplanar cavity eccentricity at end of simulation (3500 orbits)

evidence.quote: At the end of our simulations, after 3500 orbits, the cavity eccentricity has grown up to $\sim 0.4$
almost circular cavity of the size of 3 $a_{\rm{mis}}$, corresponding to $\sim 180$ au

findings_qualitative.value: Astrometry alone cannot break degeneracy between coplanar and misaligned orbits, but modest misalignment is probable

evidence.quote: are not capable of fully breaking the degeneracy between families of coplanar and misaligned orbits, but obtaining that a modest misalignment is probable

claims.hypothesis: Is the GG Tau A orbit coplanar or misaligned with the circumtriple ring?
claims.result: Delta theta ~12 deg preferred by MCMC, but degeneracy remains

evidence.quote: we conclude, albeit tentatively, that a modest degree of misalignment is preferred by the currently available astrometric data

claims.hypothesis: Which simulated configuration matches the ALMA and SPHERE morphology?
claims.experiment: Compare synthetic MCFOST images of coplanar and misaligned snapshots with data
claims.result: Misaligned on short timescales matches; coplanar fails at both times
claims.finding: Misaligned configuration (shorter than tau_ecc) is best match

evidence.loc: What is the most likely configuration for GG Tau A?
evidence.quote: We conclude that the misaligned configuration on short times is the best match of GG Tau A.

claims.hypothesis: Does disc eccentricity growth occur and conflict with observation?
claims.result: Cavity grows and becomes eccentric beyond tau_ecc, no longer matching
claims.finding: Either system younger than tau_ecc or growth suppressed

evidence.quote: This implies that either the age of the system is shorter than $\tau_{ecc}$ or that the disc eccentricity growth is not triggered or dissipated in the system.

why_this_method.value: Astrometry does not constrain orbit, so simulation morphology compared to observations is used

evidence.quote: As our new astrometric data points do not completely constrain the orbits of the system, we rely on the comparison between the morphology of the outcomes of numerical simulations and observations

limitations_admitted.value: Models do not fully reproduce SPHERE morphology; comparison is qualitative, deferred to future work

evidence.quote: We therefore defer to a future work a more quantitative characterisation of the observed features.

referee_caveats_inferred: Comparison with ALMA is visual, no quantitative metric
Only one grain size and two orbits tested; a small parameter space
Viscosity and tau_ecc dependence not explored
